rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods <U+2013> 2-year outdoor pot experiment (1998, 1999) on autumn-sown sugar beet with three drip-irrigation frequencies (SWD1 30%, SWD2 50%, SWD3 70% of TAW), soil moisture monitored by TDR, RWU and RLD measured, randomised block design with four replications.
rows.notes: The study does not report the effect named in the passage. It did not measure root-zone water tension (matric potential); it measured volumetric soil water content by TDR, and that content was not stable: before each irrigation <U+03B8> was close to wilting point (15.5%) in the top 0.2 m for all treatments and in the 0.6<U+2013>1.0 m layer fell to 18.7% under the 9-day interval (Figure 3a, Results). What the study actually shows is that total daily root water uptake per plant did not differ significantly among irrigation intervals (1471 to 1410 mL/day, Table 3) because the plants shifted uptake to deeper layers (60% from 0.6<U+2013>1.0 m under SWD3) with more efficient deeper roots and a higher root/shoot ratio, i.e. insensitivity to interval was attributed to root acclimation, not to buffered soil water tension. The system was surface drip (one line, two 2 L/h drippers per pot), not subsurface drip, though the passage names subsurface drip only as an example of micro-irrigation, so no technology mismatch is flagged. Yield was not measured (pots, one plant each).

notes: Full text available including tables; figures described in captions only. Study is a pot experiment at one site, one soil, one cultivar, two years; dispersion reported as standard errors for RWU and RLD (Tables 3 and 4), but these concern uptake and root density, not the claimed stable water tension.
